Cloud infrastructure for staging/CI environment (build minutes, hosting, staging DB) - first 3 months
Data migration tooling / temporary Oracle-to-target ETL environment (PW-8)

assumptions: The rate card provided is a PLACEHOLDER: a single generic 'Team member' role at $75/hr with 1 FTE. No real roles (e.g. developer, QA, PM, designer) or differentiated rates have been assigned yet. This estimate is therefore indicative only and MUST be revisited once actual team composition and rates are known - true costs could differ substantially depending on seniority mix and specialisation.

With only 1 FTE available, this backlog (167 story points across 24 tasks) represents a very large amount of work for a single person. At a rough industry rule of thumb of ~6-8 hours per story point for a solo generalist handling design, build, test and deployment, total effort is estimated at roughly 2,880 hours (~1.4 person-years of full-time work for one person, i.e. approximately 18 months at 40 hrs/week including some ramp-up/context-switch overhead).

No historical actuals (real spend data) exist for this project yet, so this estimate is based purely on backlog sizing (story points) and generic effort heuristics, not on observed team velocity or past delivery costs.

Because there is only 1 FTE, work must be fully serialised; there is no parallelisation of frontend/backend/QA streams, which increases calendar time (not cost) significantly and increases delivery risk since there is no redundancy if the person is unavailable.

Given the single generic role, all hours (design, engineering, testing, DevOps, data migration, accessibility, etc.) are bundled into one 'Team member' labour line rather than split across specialist roles, since no other roles exist on the rate card.

Non-labour costs are rough placeholders for third-party services (Stripe, email delivery, search indexing), CI/staging infrastructure, migration tooling, and an external accessibility audit; actual figures depend on vendor selection and usage volumes not yet known.

Story points were converted to hours using an approximate blended rate of 7 hours/point (adjusted slightly up for high-complexity/high-risk items like PW-7, PW-8, PW-14 and down for simpler items like PW-23, PW-24), then rounded to the nearest reasonable total per priority band.

Priority breakdown totals are derived by summing the estimated labour cost of tasks in each priority band, using the same $75/hr rate; they do not include non-labour costs which are allocated separately.

It is assumed the 1 FTE has the necessary skill breadth (full-stack engineering, DevOps, basic UX, data migration, and security) to complete all backlog items without needing to subcontract additional skilled roles beyond the listed non-labour third-party services.
input.reasoning: "Total backlog size is 167 story points across 24 tasks spanning setup/infra, security-critical features (auth, RBAC, 2FA, payments), core customer-facing functionality (dashboard, invoices, search, multi-currency), compliance (GDPR, accessibility), a large legacy data migration, and several lower-priority admin/reporting/decommissioning items. With only a single generic 'Team member' role available on the rate card at $75/hr and 1 FTE, I converted story points to hours using a blended heuristic of ~7 hours per point (higher for complex/risky items such as payment integration and data migration, lower for simple items such as contract tests and decommissioning), yielding a most-likely total of about 2,880 hours ($216,000). A pessimistic scenario (+~32%) accounts for the well-known risks of legacy data migration, third-party payment integration, and multi-currency correctness, plus the fact a single-person team has no slack for illness, rework or scope discovery. An optimistic scenario (-~24%) assumes the backlog is well-understood, low rework, and some low-priority items are descoped early. Because the rate card is explicitly a placeholder, the dollar figures should be treated as rough sizing only until real roles/rates are assigned; the estimate is more useful currently as a relative sizing exercise (in hours) than as a firm budget number. Non-labour costs are modest placeholders for infrastructure, third-party services and one external audit, since a solo/small setup won't need heavy license/tooling spend beyond essentials."

reductions.description: Descope PW-18 (Admin back-office for support staff), PW-19 (Usage analytics/reporting) and PW-23 (Contract tests against helpdesk API) from this phase - all Low priority, ~26 points combined - and revisit in a later phase.
reductions.effect: Removes ~360 hours of lower-priority work; reduces near-term delivery risk given the single-FTE constraint, at the cost of deferring internal support tooling and CSV reporting.

reductions.description: Defer PW-24 (Decommission legacy portal) and PW-12 (Support ticket submission) - Low priority, 13 points combined - until after the core portal is live, since the legacy system can keep running in parallel initially.
reductions.effect: Removes ~180 hours from the current scope; legacy infra costs continue a bit longer but launch-critical work is prioritized.

reductions.description: Simplify PW-14 (Multi-currency support) to a single settlement currency (USD) with display-only FX conversion for EUR/PLN in this phase, rather than full multi-currency settlement.
reductions.effect: Cuts an estimated ~160 hours of complex FX/settlement logic and testing; full settlement in EUR/PLN can be added in a later release once transaction volume justifies it.

reductions.description: Reduce PW-15 (Accessibility pass) scope to WCAG 2.2 AA on customer-facing critical paths only (login, dashboard, invoices, payments) rather than all screens including internal/admin ones, and drop the external accessibility audit line item.
reductions.effect: Saves roughly 80 hours of engineering/design time plus the $2,500 external audit cost; broader accessibility coverage across secondary/internal screens is deferred.

reductions.description: Add a second FTE (outside current placeholder rate card) to parallelize work instead of serial single-person delivery - not a direct dollar saving, but reduces calendar time and associated schedule-risk cost/opportunity cost significantly.
reductions.effect: No direct labour-cost saving under the current placeholder rate card, but strongly recommended once real roles/rates exist, since a solo FTE delivering 167 points serially carries high schedule and single-point-of-failure risk that could translate into indirect cost overruns.
